narrative.overview: SiaSurf is a shoreline registry, not a surf brochure. The system reads as a verified ledger brought to the beach: institutional calm, stamped validation, and live accountable monitoring. Every surface balances SISA authority with island approachability — tonal sand and slate grounds, ocean/reef as the single signal of verification, and bento containers that feel lifted only when they earn attention. The philosophy is verified & sunlit. Density is composed, not crowded: wave-dividers, generous section padding (96px vertical rhythm), and rounded-[2rem] bento that breathe between tasks. Motion is ambient (wave 3s, float 6s, pulse-slow 4s, shimmer 2s) and never bounce-elastic; verification is tactile — badges, QR seals, and countdown bars — not decorative chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Ledger-first: bento cards, audit tables, and real-time streams over marketing gloss
Ocean-led signal: neutral grounds carried by sand/slate, ocean/reef reserved for verified state
Soft-layered lift: flat at rest, ambient shadow+lift on interaction
Tactile & verified: pill badges, stamp-like verification, and human-readable safety copy
Mobile beach to desktop watchtower: same tokens, rhythmic density shifts

rules.name: The One Verification Color Rule
rules.body: Only ocean/reef may signal verified/live/success. Sand, slate, wave, and rose never borrow that meaning; a teal badge off-system is a defect.

rules.name: The Sand Ground Rule
rules.body: Neutral grounds are tinted sand/slate, never pure gray. Gray washes verification; sand tints it.

rules.name: The 12% Cap Rule
rules.body: Saturated ocean/reef fields occupy ≤12% of any viewport; rarity is the trust signal.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy via weight 400→700→900 and tracking, not a new family. Introducing a new display face requires an explicit ledger reason.

rules.name: The Cinzel Seal Rule
rules.body: Cinzel appears ≤1× per viewport, as a seal or ceremony; running headings stay Outfit.

rules.name: The Lift Means Live Rule
rules.body: Shadows/glow signal live/verified/hover only. A static marketing card with persistent glow is a defect.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Interiors of registry tables and forms sit tonal and flat; depth is reserved for container state, not chrome.

dos: Do keep verification pill-first (rounded-full, backdrop-blur-md, CheckBadgeIcon) — its calm stamp is the trust signal.
Do use weight+tracking for hierarchy (900 + tracking-widest at 10px) over new families; check flat-type-hierarchy detector before adding a size.
Do pair white cards on sand grounds (bg-white on bg-sand-50/bg-slate-50); the tint carries the island light.
Do animate with wave/float/pulse-slow/shimmer + ease-out-quart only; no animate-bounce.
Do resolve every gray-on-color finding: gray text on bg-teal-*/bg-rose-* becomes text-white, text-slate-900, or darker tint of the field.
donts: Don't add border-l-4 side-tab accents to cards or nav — 4 files flagged; use pill or tonal fill instead.
Don't place gray text on colored fields (text-gray-400 on bg-green-500 etc.) or text-slate-400 on bg-rose-600.
Don't use animate-bounce or elastic/bounce easing — decelerate smoothly.
Don't add marketing buzzwords (world-class, streamline, enterprise-grade) to copy.
Don't add numbered section markers 01/02/03 or new Playfair/Inter-as-display faces — Outfit carries display, Cinzel only as seal.
Don't nest cards in cards for sake of enclosure; flatten parent to bg-slate-50 and let child be the signal.
